gaps.note: HIG section 8 says 'there are two locations on the case in which the grounding lug may be fixed', and Figure 22 draws both on one unlabelled flank: Location-1 just behind the front face, drawn here as one M4 pair, and Location-2 about 194 and 209 mm behind it, which is not drawn yet. Which flank the figure shows is not stated; the right is taken from the Figure 5 inset.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the real unit flanks, or a figure captioned with the side

gaps.note: No held document dimensions the two grounding holes. The hardware installation guide names the screws (two M4) and the accessory lug (50 x 11.1 x 7.5 mm, #6 AWG) and draws the holes; the flank figure reads 15.6 to 15.9 apart, and the pair is drawn at the 5/8 in. (15.875) that reading and the two-hole lug both point at.
gaps.wanted: a drawing that dimensions the grounding holes, or the accessory lug's own datasheet

gaps.note: HIG section 10 tables the five system lamps (GNSS, SYNC, STAT, FAN, PWR), the PSU and Fan FRU lamps and the management jack, and gives no table at all for the port lamps. Figure 9 draws an up/down green pair in the web of every SFP+ and SFP28 column and two lamps in the QSFP28 web, so which port each lamp belongs to is clear from the arrows; what its colours and behaviours MEAN is not stated. Every port lamp therefore keeps common/led-dot's off/on default rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary. The same guide annotates nine rows of the system-lamp tables 'need NOS to activate this feature', so these may be NOS-defined rather than merely undocumented - which is a different fix, and the reason this is vendor-silent rather than nos-dependent.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states

gaps.note: HIG Figure 9 draws the ganged shells 25.5 mm tall, which cannot hold two 10.4 mm SFP openings on any manufacturable belly-to-belly pitch; the front photograph and std/sfp-ganged's own TE-measured 15.00 mm row pitch require 27.6 mm. The manifest carries 27.6 and the 15.0 mm pitch, and the whole port band therefore sits 1.05 mm higher at the top and 1.05 mm lower at the bottom than the guide figure draws it. The figure had already failed the aspect gate by 2.1 percent in the same direction, which is why the photograph was preferred rather than split the difference.
gaps.wanted: a vendor mechanical drawing of the faceplate, or a caliper on the shell

gaps.note: Each fan carries a two-line legend on the chassis web beside it - the word FAN over an arrow and one digit - in the same position and the same form as the S9301-32D's rear. At the rear render's 1.168 px/mm the digit is not legible at any zoom, so the numbering is carried 0-based to match this device's own port table (0~3, 4~11, 12~19, 20~21) and the S9301-32D's rear rail, and NOT the sibling S9510-28DC, which prints FAN-1 to FAN-5 and is 1-based. Two house precedents disagree and no held image of this device settles it. The legend is also not DRAWN on the faceplate: it sits inside the module's own flange area and the chassis web between bays is 0.9 mm, so a chassis mark there would be painted over by the seated fan. The group numbering carries the fact; the drawing does not.
gaps.wanted: a legible photograph of the rear fan bays, or a rear elevation figure

gaps.note: Searched and absent, and this is the SAME silence the sibling S9510-28DC already records for the same fan rather than a second independent reading: the HIG dimensions and weighs the fan FRU (51.5 x 57.8 x 42.2 mm, 90 g) and tables its LED without ever stating a wattage, and this device's own datasheet names FAN-402825-HD only as an ordering line. The PSUs are sourced from their model numbers (PSU-201, 200 W); the fan has no equivalent, so L29 stands and the chassis module total is a floor.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the fan module's label, or a UfiSpace FRU datasheet

gaps.note: No held document prints an orderable chassis part number - the datasheet and the HIG name only S9500-22XST, and the Available to Order section names only PSU-201-DISB, PSU-201-AISB and FAN-402825-HD. Per the S9510-28DC precedent in this library, whose -BN0B and -BR1B SKUs surfaced from the owner and from no PDF, orderable SKUs for the AC and DC builds exist somewhere; the configurations therefore carry no part-numbers rather than invented ones.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace ordering guide or a quote naming the chassis SKUs

gaps.note: The five system lamps measure 3.3 x 3.0 mm in Figure 9 and the library's nearest part, common/led-rect@1, is 4.6 x 2.6 - wider and shorter than the drawn lamp. It is used here because it is what the sibling S9510-28DC carries for the identical five-lamp row and because this device may not add components, but on the measured 6.85 mm pitch it closes the printed gap between neighbours from 3.5 mm to 2.25 mm.
gaps.wanted: a square ~3.2 mm indicator component, or a caliper on the lamp window

attrs.note: datasheet - Physical, Performance, Environmental, Regulatory Compliance, Timing and Accessories sections, transcribed into sections. Compliance strings kept verbatim and semicolon-separated, untidied. The datasheet's key-features list prints 'IEEE 1558v2' where every other line in the same document and the timing row itself print IEEE 1588v2; the obvious typo is not propagated and 1588v2 is carried.

cage-mirroring.note: photo-measured, and it says the stacked optical rows are NOT belly-to-belly. Rotating a std/sfp-ganged moves its drawn cavity 1.13 mm across the 10.4 mm opening, so the apparent pitch between the two rows' dark cavities is 15.0 mm if the rows share an orientation and 12.7 or 17.3 mm if they mirror. The front photograph rendered to the same 8 px/mm as the model gives 15.4 mm; the first draft, with the lower row turned 180, rendered 12.65. Both SFP+ and SFP28 rows are therefore drawn unmirrored, and declared so in stack-exceptions. The QSFP28 pair cannot be tested this way - std/qsfp28's cavity is symmetric, so the test is blind to it - and with no reading of its own it follows the library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S3: upper rotate 0 over lower 180, both bails outward), the lower cage rotate 180. That is the rule, not an observation, and the unmirrored SFP rows beside it are a reason to photograph it.

chassis.note: datasheet - 'Chassis (W x D x H) 1RU, 440 x 302 x 43.5 mm', weight 4.75 kg without FRU; the HIG Component Physical Information table repeats the same triple (17.32" x 11.89" x 1.71") and gives 4.75 kg. NOTE the sibling S9510-28DC carries 4.9 kg for the same 440 x 302 x 43.5 body - that is a different product's figure, not a disagreement about this one. 440 is the body: the HIG ships a separate 50.4 x 43 x 20 mm rack mount bracket as accessory 3, so the 19 inch mounting hardware is additional to 440 and is not drawn. The Figure 5 depth dimension confirms 302 mm for the chassis and calls out 327.4 mm over the projecting PSU handles (27 mm).

front-layout.note: drawing - HIG Figure 9 at 8.559 px/mm, measured on the 600 dpi page render; x positions good to about 0.3 mm, y taken from the photograph per the front-vertical note. Left to right: PSU0 and PSU1 front-service bays on a measured 58.77 mm pitch; the system-lamp row and the timing block (five SMA jacks, the BITS/ToD stack); the management stack (RJ45 out-of-band, USB 2.0 Type-A, RJ45 console) with a micro-USB console beside it; then the four port blocks, each in its own silver ganged shell, with honeycomb vent fields above, below and between them. Shell extents measured off the silver mask: RJ45 215.10-246.73, SFP+ 259.22-318.74, SFP28 333.45-392.97, QSFP28 409.43-430.32. Every block's flange comes out at 1.2-1.3 mm per side against the standard opening it holds, which is the check that the shells and the parts agree.

front-vertical.note: THE FIGURE AND THE PHOTOGRAPH DISAGREE HERE AND THE PHOTOGRAPH WINS. All four port blocks share one vertical band. Figure 9 draws the ganged shells spanning y 9.4-34.9 (25.5 mm), which leaves room for two 10.4 mm SFP openings only on a 12.7 mm belly-to-belly pitch - a 2.3 mm web, which no stacked SFP cage has. The front photograph, whose apertures are real holes rather than drawn module faces, shows the silver web between the rows spanning 5.1 mm and the openings centred 14.6 mm apart; 5.1 mm of web with 10.4 mm openings IS the standard 15.0 mm pitch that std/sfp-ganged's own contract records as measured from a TE 2007562-6 cage. So the rows are modelled at a 15.0 mm pitch and the shells are 27.6 mm tall - 2.1 mm taller than Figure 9 draws them, which is the same 2 percent the aspect gate already caught, in the same direction. The other three blocks are centred on the same two row centres because the photograph shows one continuous silver band across all four. THE WHOLE BAND WAS THEN MOVED DOWN 0.8 mm by the matched-scale comparison: rendered at the photograph's own 8 px/mm, the first draft's apertures sat 0.5, 0.95 and 1.0 mm high on the RJ45, SFP+ and QSFP28 blocks respectively - three independent blocks, all the same direction - so 0.8 mm was taken off the whole band rather than any one block. Final openings: SFP rows at y 10.35 and 25.25, the 1G jacks at 10.05 and 24.95, the QSFP28 pair at 10.48 and 25.38, shells 9.2-36.8. The residual is about 0.85 mm, which is one pixel of the photograph and the honest limit of this face's vertical placement.

ground-pair.note: ONE TWO-HOLE LANDING, NOT TWO SCREWS (#830). The accessory grounding lug (50 x 11.1 x 7.5 mm, #6 AWG) is fixed with two M4 screws, so the point is common/ground-stud-pair-5-8-m4@1, two M4 pan heads on 5/8 in. (15.875) centres, unturned because the holes lie along the depth. MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: HIG Figure 22, the flank elevation section 8 draws for this chassis, measured on the docling figure (910 x 446 px, an upsample of the 544 x 266 px image the PDF embeds): chassis bar x 76.5 to 843 px for the 302 mm depth, 2.54 px/mm, and 111 px for the 43.5 mm height. The two M4 holes of Location-1 centre at 97.6 and 137.6 px, y 121 px, so the holes sit 8.3 and 24.1 mm behind the front face, 15.76 mm apart, centred 16.2 from the front and 22 from the top. The same accessory lug, read the same way on THREE DISTINCT DRAWINGS ACROSS SEVEN GUIDES (one 544 x 266 image shared byte for byte by the S9500-22XST, S9501-28SMT, S9510-28DC and S9510-30XC guides as Figure 22, one shared by the M3000-14XC and S9502-16SMT guides, and Figure 15 of the S9511-20CT guide alone), gives 15.6 to 15.9, against about 0.65 mm per pixel of the embedded art: the 5/8 in. two-hole pattern. AXIS: x = 0 is the FRONT on a right view, and the front is the left end of the figure, as on ufispace/s9501-18smt. Formerly two common/ground-lug@1 placements, ground-1 and ground-2, at x 40 and 51 at y 15 (studs 11.0 apart, centred 45.5 from the front).

ground-stud-size.note: the hardware installation guide lists, in its package contents, a screw kit for the grounding lug of 2 x M4*L8.0mm screws, and its grounding steps lock the grounding lug to the designated grounding location with 2 M4 screws: the `stud-size` of ground-screws, the pair. The accessory lug is one two-hole lug held by both screws.

jack-orientation.note: THE FIRST DRAFT HAD THIS BACKWARDS ON THE 1G BLOCK AND THE MATCHED-SCALE RENDER CAUGHT IT, so both readings are recorded. std/rj45-ganged draws the latch keyway DOWN and its gold contacts at the TOP, and on a real jack the integrated lamps sit at the contact end, opposite the latch. The four 100M/1G jacks show their lamps at the TOP corners on the upper row and the BOTTOM corners on the lower, so the UPPER row is unrotated and the LOWER carries rotate: 180 - the reverse of what this file first said, which had reasoned from common/rj45-port@4 (a different part, which composes std/rj45 already turned 180) and got the sense inverted. What settled it was measuring the rendered contact band against the photograph's at 8 px/mm: the vendor's upper jacks have their contacts high and the lower jacks low, and the first draft rendered the opposite. The two stacked TIMING jacks were read directly from the silhouette at 7x and are genuinely mirrored the other way - BITS above with its latch notch UP (rotate: 180), ToD below with it down - as is the management stack, whose top out-of-band RJ45 is keyway-up with its green lamp at the top right and whose bottom console RJ45 is keyway-down.

lifecycle.note: searched 2026-08-28: 'UfiSpace S9500-22XST end of life end of sale' - no announcement found; the vendor product page and the datasheet PDF are live and distributor listings carry it. none-announced is a real finding here, not an absence of looking.

mgmt-block.note: drawing - one 15.77 mm silver shell at x 184.17 holding, top to bottom, the 100/1000M out-of-band RJ45, a USB 2.0 Type-A and the RS-232 console RJ45; the silver cross-bars inside it were measured at y 6.41-7.10, 16.60-19.00, 24.38-27.13 and 35.60-36.97 and the three parts are centred in the openings between them. The micro-USB console sits separately at x 166.10 under its own IOIO legend, with the network symbol beside it; the datasheet lists it as one port - '1 x RJ45 & Micro USB serial console port' - so the RJ45 console and the micro-USB are two connectors on one interface and are grouped together. Legends 'IOIO' above and the USB/arrow/IOIO line below the stack are transcribed as printed.

part-numbers.note: The FRU ordering lines are the datasheet's own: PSU-201-DISB (200 W DC, intake air flow), PSU-201-AISB (200 W AC, intake air flow) and FAN-402825-HD (exhaust air flow). Only ONE fan SKU is listed, so unlike the vendor's data-centre boxes this product line offers no back-to-front airflow variant in any held document. NO ORDERABLE CHASSIS SKU appears anywhere in the datasheet or the HIG; per the S9510-28DC precedent in this library - whose -BN0B and -BR1B SKUs came from the owner and from no PDF - that is recorded as a gap rather than as 'no SKU exists'.

port-lamps.note: drawing - each SFP+ and SFP28 column carries a green up/down lamp PAIR in the silver web between its two rows (four pairs per block, read at 2.2x), so one lamp serves the upper port and one the lower; the QSFP28 stack carries two lamps in the same position. What they mean is not stated anywhere - see the port-led-semantics gap - so every one keeps common/led-dot's off/on default. The four 100M/1G jacks carry their lamps inside the jack, which is why they are not placed separately.

port-numbers.note: drawing - the HIG port table numbers the faceplate 0~3 RJ45, 4~11 SFP+, 12~19 SFP28, 20~21 QSFP28, and Figure 9 prints each number twice: once LARGE on the drawn module face, where a seated transceiver would cover it, and once SMALL on the metal above or below its block. The small marks are the silkscreen and are what is modelled, at baselines 7.9 (upper row) and 37.9 (lower). On the SFP28 block those marks sit on yellow printed bands - measured at x 334.5-392.7, y 6.2-8.4 and 36.0-38.2 - which are faceplate paint and are drawn as panel.decor so the numbers print over them. The other three blocks have no band and their numbers are white on bare metal.

power.note: datasheet 'Typical power: 111.8 Watts (no transceiver)' - the vendor's own scope, so power-envelope is bare. NO MAXIMUM IS PUBLISHED: the HIG's Connecting Power section gives wiring and breaker instructions and states no system wattage, and the datasheet prints only the typical figure and the per-feed input ratings (AC 100-240 V 3 A, DC -36 to -75 V 8 A). power-max-w is therefore absent rather than derived from the input ratings, which would be a supply-side number wearing a draw-side key.

rear-layout.note: photo-measured - no held figure draws the rear elevation, so it is taken from the rear product render at 1.168 px/mm (width-derived; that photograph's own aspect is 11 percent out because the panel detection catches its drop shadow, so only x is used from it and the module height comes from the HIG table). Three fan faces measured at 71.7-123.7, 124.4-175.8 and 176.5-228.6 mm - 51.4 to 52.1 mm wide against the HIG table's 51.5 mm fan module, on a 52.4 mm pitch - with plain chassis to their left and a honeycomb vent field at 285-422 mm, flat chassis either side of it. That vent extent was re-measured against the photograph at matched scale after the first render put its left edge 45 mm too far in; the flat panel left of fan 0 carries a faint vertical seam that no held document identifies, so nothing is drawn there rather than guessing at a cover. The three measured pitches came out at 52.7 and 52.1 mm, a 0.6 mm disagreement at a photograph resolving 0.86 mm per pixel - noise, not a stagger - so the bays sit on one 52.4 mm pitch rather than recording an unevenness the source cannot support. Each fan's airflow tag, captive screw and status lamp sit on the module, as ufispace/fan-402825@1 draws them. NO FAN LEGEND IS DRAWN as chassis silkscreen: the 'FAN <n>' mark sits inside the module's own right-hand flange area on the hardware, and the chassis web between bays measures 0.9 mm, so there is nowhere on the metal to print it that a seated module would not paint over. See the fan-numbering gap.

rj45-pitch.note: measured, AND IT IS NOT THE PART'S OWN PITCH. The four 100M/1G jacks sit two wide in a 31.63 mm shell; taking the same 1.27 mm flange the other blocks show leaves 29.09 mm for two columns, so the vendor's column pitch is 14.55 mm. std/rj45-ganged is 12.7 mm wide - the per-port aperture of a block whose instances abut - so the two jacks here do NOT abut: they are centred in their columns at 217.30 and 231.84, leaving 1.85 mm of shell between them. That was cross-checked against the drawn jack faces in Figure 9 at 3.5x (218.5-230.7 and 232.5-244.7), which agree to 1.2 mm. The silver strips are drawn as panel.decor per the S9510-28DC precedent, because std/rj45-ganged draws the opening only.

sources.note: UfiSpace S9500-22XST datasheet for dimensions, weight, port inventory, platform, timing, power, environment, compliance and the FRU ordering lines; S9500-22XST Hardware Installation Guide (s9500-22xst-hig) for the Port Overview elevation, the Component Physical Information table, the Figure 5 overview drawing, the LED tables, grounding and rack mounting; three vendor product renders (photos/s9500-22xst-1-angle, -2-front, -3-rear) for colour, counts, construction, and for two measurements the drawings could not settle. FIGURE QUALITY WAS GATED FIRST AND ONE FIGURE FAILED. The HIG Port Overview (Figure 9, page 12 of the PDF at 600 dpi) measures 3766 x 380 px across the 440 x 43.5 mm face: aspect 9.90 against a true 10.115, 2.1 percent out, so it is NOT orthographic and its absolute vertical scale is not used. Its horizontal scale is trusted, and was validated rather than assumed - at 8.559 px/mm the SFP+ ganged shell measures 59.52 mm, which is 4 x 14.25 (the SFF-8433 port pitch) plus a 1.26 mm flange each side, and the PSU latch-to-latch pitch comes out at 58.77 mm against the 58.7 mm the sibling S9510-28DC carries for the same PSU form factor. The Figure 5 top-view drawing on page 10 DOES pass: 2182 x 1488 px against 440 x 302 mm is aspect 1.466 versus a true 1.457, 0.6 percent, so the top face is measured rather than proportioned.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the rule, not an observation, so a photograph of the stack overturns it: the 1 QSFP pair (port-20/port-21). Declared in stack-exceptions with the reading that keeps them otherwise: the 8 SFP pairs (port-4/port-5 to port-18/port-19). The QSFP28 pair has no reading of its own - the cavity-pitch test is blind to std/qsfp28's symmetric cavity - so it takes the rule, and the unmirrored SFP rows beside it are a reason to photograph it.

system-lamps.note: drawing - five lamps on a regularised 6.85 mm pitch at x centres 134.37, 141.22, 148.07, 154.92 and 161.77, y centre 9.62, under the printed RST GNSS SYNC STAT FAN PWR row at baseline 6.2. The individual measured pitches ran 6.66-6.95 and were put on one pitch rather than drawn staggered, per the house rule for a lamp row that shares a baseline on the real device. THE LAMPS ARE DRAWN WIDER THAN THEY MEASURE: the green fill measures 3.3 x 3.0 mm and common/led-rect@1 is 4.6 x 2.6, which is the closest part in the library and the one the sibling S9510-28DC uses for this same five-lamp row; on a 6.85 mm pitch it leaves a 2.25 mm gap rather than the drawn 3.5 mm. Said here because nothing else records it. LED semantics from the HIG section 10 tables.

timing-block.note: drawing - five SMA jacks, measured from the gold mask as three columns at x 125.30, 140.20 and 155.20 (14.95 mm pitch, 9.8 mm outside diameter against common/sma-jack's 9.5) on two rows at y centres 16.98 and 29.93. The left column carries only the lower jack, which is GNSS ANT; the other two columns carry 1PPS IN/OUT above and 10MHZ IN/OUT below, exactly as the printed legends run - IN, 1PPS, OUT under the top row and GNSS ANT, IN, 10MHZ, OUT under the bottom. The datasheet's timing list (1x GNSS input SMA, 1x 1PPS input/output SMA, 1x 10MHz input/output SMA) reads as three interfaces and the faceplate has five jacks, because the in/out pairs are two connectors each; that is not a conflict and both are recorded. BITS is on RJ48 and ToD on RJ45 per the datasheet, stacked in one 15.07 mm shell under the printed 'BITS (up)(down) TOD'.

views.note: Six views. TOP: y = 0 is the REAR, per the house convention and the HIG Figure 5 drawing, which prints the projecting red fan handles at its top edge and the blue PSU latches at its bottom; that drawing passes the aspect gate at 0.6 percent, so the two long stadium reliefs and the four short ones are measured from it rather than proportioned. BOTTOM mirrors left-right and carries the compliance sticker at an estimated position. LEFT (x = 0 is the REAR) and RIGHT (x = 0 is the FRONT): the HIG section 8 puts the grounding lug on the side of the chassis and the Figure 5 callout inset shows it on the RIGHT side near the front, which is where the two-hole lug is drawn - the one asymmetric feature on either side face, and the reason the depth-axis convention on those two views is load-bearing here rather than merely stated. Screw positions on both side faces are estimated; no drawing dimensions them.
